To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the backpropagation algorithm can be extended to recurrent networks in a straightforward manner, that this algorithm has a very large computational requirement for training, that a number of other algorithms can be used to adjust weights in recurrent networks and that these other algorithms have much lower computational requirements.
(1) gradient-based learning algorithms are possible for recurrent networks, (2) these algorithms are computationally expensive, and (3) they are not always guaranteed to converge.

the backpropagation through time (BPTT) algorithm is computationally the most expensive, the real time recurrent learning (RTRL) algorithm is computational the cheapest, the Kalman filter approach is computationally intermediate, and the Kalman filter is the only algorithm of those examined that can be implemented in parallel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a set of tools for training recurrent connectionist networks to perform temporal mappings.
the following questions: How can we learn to produce desired temporal patterns in recurrent networks?
the development of a set of techniques for learning recurrent connectionist networks, and with an evaluation of the computational complexity of these techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gradient-based learning algorithms for dynamic recurrent networks have been studied and understood to a degree that makes it clear that they will be useful and important tools for training recurrent networks for many tasks.

gradient-based learning is possible for recurrent connectionist nets, that it is computationally feasible for many practical problems, and that there is a large number of different ways of implementing gradient computation for such networks.

the gradient approach is the best approach for learning in recurrent connectionist networks and that the computational requirements of gradient learning in recurrent networks are quite reasonable and manageable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a number of techniques for training recurrent connectionist networks to perform temporal pattern processing tasks.

we are now able to compute the gradient for a recurrent connectionist network in time proportional to the number of connections in the network and the number of gradient computations to be made, rather than the number of connections multiplied by the number of gradient calculations.
the back-propagation algorithm for recurrent networks is computationally expensive and has some signicant drawbacks.

there are a number of ways in which one can compute the gradient of performance with respect to network parameters.

the gradient-based learning algorithms are very practical and effective in a wide variety of recurrent connectionist networks, and can be applied to networks with many hidden units and long temporal delays.
